Background Growth hormone (GH) resistance is characterized by high GH levels but low levels of insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) and growth hormone binding protein (GHBP) and, for patients with chronic disease, is associated with the development of cachexia. Objectives We investigated whether GH resistance is associated with changes in left ventricular (LV) mass (cardiac wasting) in patients with cancer. Methods We measured plasma IGF-I, GH, and GHBP in 159 women and 148 men with cancer (83% stage III/IV). Patients were grouped by tertile of echocardiographic LVmass/height 2 (women, < 50, 50–61, > 61 g/m 2 ; men, < 60, 60–74, > 74 g/m 2 ) and by presence of wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss (BMI < 24 kg/m 2 and weight loss ≥ 5% in the prior 12 months). Repeat echocardiograms were obtained usually within 3–6 months for 85 patients. Results Patients in the lowest LVmass/height 2 tertile had higher plasma GH (median (IQR) for 1 st , 2 nd , and 3 rd tertile women, 1.8 (0.9–4.2), 0.8 (0.2–2.2), 0.5 (0.3–1.6) ng/mL, p = 0.029; men, 2.1 (0.8–3.2), 0.6 (0.1–1.7), 0.7 (0.2–1.9) ng/mL, p = 0.003). Among women, lower LVmass was associated with higher plasma IGF-I (68 (48–116), 72 (48–95), 49 (35–76) ng/mL, p = 0.007), whereas such association did not exist for men. Patients with lower LVmass had lower log IGF-I/GH ratio (women, 1.60 ± 0.09, 2.02 ± 0.09, 1.88 ± 0.09, p = 0.004; men, 1.64 ± 0.09, 2.14 ± 0.11, 2.04 ± 0.11, p = 0.002). GHBP was not associated with LVmass. Patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss had higher plasma GH and GHBP, lower log IGF-I/GH ratio, and similar IGF-I. Overall, GHBP correlated inversely with log IGF-I/GH ratio (women, r = − 0.591, p < 0.001; men, r = − 0.575, p < 0.001). Additionally, higher baseline IGF-I was associated with a decline in LVmass during follow-up ( r = − 0.318, p = 0.003). Conclusion In advanced cancer, reduced LVmass is associated with increased plasma GH and reduced IGF-I/GH ratio, suggesting increasing GH resistance, especially for patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss. Higher baseline IGF-I was associated with a decrease in relative LVmass during follow-up. Keywords Left ventricular mass Growth hormone Insulin-like growth factor-I Cardiology Cancer Echocardiography Cachexia http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/100010447 Deutsches Zentrum für Herz-Kreislaufforschung 81Z0710102 Zeller Tanja Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin (3093) Open Access funding enabled and organized by Projekt DEAL. issue-copyright-statement © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2025 Introduction Cardiac wasting–associated cardiomyopathy has recently been described in patients with advanced-stage cancer [ 1 , 2 ] and was shown to be associated with reduced physical performance, increased all-cause mortality, and inflammation. In preclinical models, the loss of left ventricular (LV) mass has been attributed to cytokine-mediated inflammatory processes and malnutrition [ 2 , 3 ]. The pathophysiological process in humans causing a remodelling process in the heart as well as an absolute decline of heart muscle tissue remains to be established. Chronic illnesses such as heart failure (HF) and cancer are often characterized by enhanced catabolism and malnutrition predisposing to loss of skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia) and loss of fat and lean muscle mass with global weight loss (cachexia). The GH-IGF-I axis is an important regulator of the wasting processes in chronic heart failure [ 4 – 7 ]. The GH-IGF-I axis consists of a complex interplay of several stages in this hormonal system (Fig. 1 ) [ 5 , 8 ]. Growth hormone (GH) is periodically released from the pituitary gland and leads to the activation of both lipolysis and anabolic effects in the body, affecting men and women similarly. GH’s main anabolic mediator is insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) that is mainly bound to IGF-Binding Protein 3 (IGFBP3) when circulating in the blood. GH itself is an important anabolic hormone that mediates several cardiometabolic processes but requires an adequate IGF-I response. Growth hormone binding protein (GHBP) is a surrogate marker for the amount of cellular GH receptors. Derived by proteolytic cleavage of the extracellular binding domain of the GH receptor, GHBP is structurally identical to the GH receptor ectodomain, and therefore both (GH receptor and GHBP) are in constant competition for GH. Depending on feedback mechanisms, GHBP can then either prolong the efficacy of GHBP-bound GH or exclude GH from binding to the GH receptor. In patients with chronic HF and GH treatment, IGF-I has been shown to positively correlate with LV mass [ 9 ]. Acquired GH resistance (as seen in cachectic HF patients) [ 10 ] is characterized by a shortage of cellular GH receptors (i.e., GHBP is reduced), elevated circulating GH, and low IGF-I [ 8 , 11 ]. GH sensitivity, as represented by the IGF-I/GH ratio, is very important as isolated IGF-I levels alone cannot be interpreted. We hypothesized that GH resistance is also important in the development of cardiac wasting and designed this study to test this hypothesis in cancer patients.

extracted_data.document_summary: This prospective single-center study investigated the relationship between an impaired Growth Hormone (GH)-Insulin-like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) axis and cardiac wasting (reduced left ventricular mass) in 307 advanced cancer patients. The findings reveal that reduced LV mass is associated with an imbalance in the GH-IGF-I axis, characterized by higher plasma GH levels and a lower IGF-I/GH ratio, suggesting acquired GH resistance. This resistance is particularly evident in patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss, and higher baseline IGF-I was associated with a subsequent decline in relative LV mass.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating GH-IGF-I axis dysregulation in advanced cancer patients; no therapeutic intervention.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational, cross-sectional, and longitudinal study (with follow-up for 85 patients) assessing baseline characteristics and follow-up changes in GH-IGF-I axis parameters. No intervention or dose was administered. Patient stratification involved grouping by echocardiographic left ventricular mass/height^2 tertiles (women: <50, 50–61, >61 g/m^2; men: <60, 60–74, >74 g/m^2) and by the presence of wasting syndrome (BMI <24 kg/m^2 and ≥5% weight loss in the prior 12 months).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in patients in the lowest LVmass/height^2 tertile (women, median (IQR) 1.8 (0.9–4.2) ng/mL vs. 0.8 (0.2–2.2) and 0.5 (0.3–1.6) ng/mL in higher tertiles (p=0.029); men, median (IQR) 2.1 (0.8–3.2) ng/mL vs. 0.6 (0.1–1.7) and 0.7 (0.2–1.9) ng/mL in higher tertiles (p=0.003)). Levels were also significantly higher in men and women with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss compared to those without. An inverse relationship was observed between GH and LV mass.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates growth, cellular reproduction, and metabolism; acts as an anabolic hormone that activates lipolysis and mediates cardiometabolic processes, requiring adequate IGF-I response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV) with reduced left ventricular mass (cardiac wasting) or presence of wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased levels indicate acquired GH resistance and a catabolic state, contributing to cardiac wasting-associated cardiomyopathy and independent loss of left ventricular mass in advanced cancer patients, especially those with wasting syndrome.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: varied; higher (in women with lower LV mass), similar (in wasting syndrome), higher baseline predicted decline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Among women, lower LV mass was associated with higher plasma IGF-I (68 (48–116) ng/mL in lowest LVmass/height^2 tertile vs. 72 (48–95) and 49 (35–76) ng/mL in higher tertiles, p=0.007); no such association for men. Levels were similar in patients with wasting syndrome. Higher baseline IGF-I (≥98.22 ng/mL) was associated with a reduction in LV mass during follow-up (r = -0.318, p=0.003).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Main anabolic mediator of Growth Hormone (GH), promoting cell growth, proliferation, tissue maintenance, and survival, influencing metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV) with reduced left ventricular mass (cardiac wasting), presence of wasting syndrome, and during follow-up for LV mass changes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: In women, higher levels are associated with lower left ventricular mass. Higher baseline levels predict a greater subsequent decline in LV mass over time, suggesting its role in cardiac wasting progression. Stable levels across LV mass tertiles and similar levels in wasting syndrome, combined with high GH, indicate impaired GH-IGF-I axis responsiveness and acquired GH resistance in advanced cancer patients.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (across LV mass tertiles); higher (in wasting syndrome); inversely correlated (with log IGF-I/GH ratio)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were mostly stable across LV mass tertiles and not significantly associated with LV mass. However, levels were significantly higher in patients with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss. GHBP correlated inversely with log IGF-I/GH ratio (women, r = -0.591, p < 0.001; men, r = -0.575, p < 0.001), with this correlation remaining significant after age adjustment.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Surrogate marker for cellular GH receptors, derived from proteolytic cleavage of the GH receptor ectodomain; binds to growth hormone in circulation, modulating its bioavailability and action.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV) with or without wasting syndrome and varying left ventricular mass.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels in patients with wasting syndrome, coupled with a negative correlation with the IGF-I/GH ratio, suggest a role in altered GH dynamics during catabolic states and support a state of acquired GH resistance in advanced cancer, although GHBP levels were not directly associated with reduced LV mass.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: log Insulin-like Growth Factor-I (IGF-I)/Growth Hormone (GH) ratio

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly lower in patients with lower LVmass/height^2 (women, 1.60 ± 0.09 vs. 2.02 ± 0.09 and 1.88 ± 0.09 in higher tertiles, p=0.004; men, 1.64 ± 0.09 vs. 2.14 ± 0.11 and 2.04 ± 0.11 in higher tertiles, p=0.002). Also significantly lower in men and women with wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss. An inverse relationship was observed with LV mass (Pearson r=0.203, p<0.001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the functional balance and responsiveness of the Growth Hormone (GH)-Insulin-like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) axis, indicating GH sensitivity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV) with reduced left ventricular mass (cardiac wasting) or presence of wasting syndrome with unintentional weight loss.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A lower ratio indicates acquired GH resistance, which is strongly associated with cardiac wasting and the progression of wasting syndrome in advanced cancer patients.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: similar (with wasting syndrome); lower (in patients with lower IGF-I); not associated (with reduced LV mass)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Similar levels were observed in patients with vs. without wasting syndrome, and no association was found with reduced LV mass. Lower levels were noted in patients grouped by lower IGF-I levels.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The most abundant IGF binding protein in serum, regulating IGF-I transport, bioavailability, and half-life by modulating its interaction with receptors.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Advanced cancer patients (mostly stage III/IV), assessed in relation to LV mass and wasting syndrome.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of IGF-I bioavailability and GH-IGF-I axis function; no significant association was found with reduced LV mass or wasting syndrome, but lower levels were noted in patients with lower IGF-I.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Tertiles for females: <50.00 g/m^2, 50.00–<61.15 g/m^2, ≥61.15 g/m^2; Tertiles for males: <59.85 g/m^2, 59.85–<74.06 g/m^2, ≥74.06 g/m^2. LV mass declined by -18.8 ± 2.6 g (i.e., -9.2 ± 1.5% SEM) over a mean follow-up of 153 ± 16 days.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the amount of cardiac muscle in the left ventricle; indicator of cardiac health and adaptation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Observed in patients with mostly advanced-stage cancer, particularly those with wasting syndrome.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced LV mass (cardiac wasting) is associated with an imbalance in the GH-IGF-I axis and suggests a form of cardiomyopathy in cancer patients.
